parsed.summary: The Lean theorem asserts that some group G is finitely presented and not `Sofic`. However, the bespoke `Sofic` class (line 25) has contradictory hypotheses `0 < ε → ε < 0 → …`, so every group satisfies it trivially. `¬ Sofic G` is therefore equivalent to False, and the target statement is false (unprovable in consistent Lean); it does not capture the paper's notion of soficity at all. Secondarily, the paper's Theorem 1.1 is about a specific group, L_{F2}(1,2)^×, while Lean only asserts existence of a finitely presented nonsofic group; finite presentability of that group is not in the excerpt.

glossary.plain: d_H(p,q) = |{y : p(y) ≠ q(y)}| / |Y| for permutations p, q of a finite set Y
A map σ : G → Sym(n), n > 0, with σ(1) = id
glossary.standard_concept: map into a finite symmetric group used in sofic approximation
glossary.note: Requiring σ(1)=id is a harmless normalization.

glossary.plain: σ is (F,ε)-good: for g,h ∈ F, d_H(σ(gh), σ(g)σ(h)) < ε; for g ∈ F with g ≠ 1, d_H(σ(g), id) > 1−ε
glossary.note: Perm multiplication is composition, so σ(g)σ(h) is the right order.

glossary.plain: For every finite F and every ε with 0<ε AND ε<0 AND ε<1, an (F,ε)-good model exists; since no ε satisfies 0<ε<0, this is vacuously true for every group
glossary.note: The extra hypothesis `ε < 0` contradicts `0 < ε`, making the class trivially satisfied by every group (presumably a typo for `ε < 1` alone).

lean_claims.plain: There exists a group G (in Type 0) that is finitely presented and does not satisfy `Sofic`. Since `Sofic` holds vacuously for every group, this is equivalent to False.

paper_claims.plain: The unit group L_{F2}(1,2)^× of the binary Leavitt algebra over F2 is not sofic.

coverage.why: Lean's Sofic is vacuous, so the Lean statement is False rather than nonsoficity. Even with a corrected definition, Lean is an existential claim about some finitely presented group, not about L_{F2}(1,2)^×. Finite presentability is not in the excerpt.

flags.explanation: The hypotheses `0 < ε → ε < 0 → ε < 1` are jointly unsatisfiable, so `Sofic G` holds for every group. Consequently `¬ Sofic G` is False and the target theorem is equivalent to False. The formal statement does not express nonsoficity in any sense; if a proof were accepted, it would indicate inconsistency or cheating.
flags.probe_idea: theorem all_sofic (G : Type) [Group G] : SoficGroups.Sofic G := ⟨fun _ ε h0 hneg _ => absurd (h0.trans hneg) (lt_irrefl 0)⟩ — then derive ¬ (target statement).

flags.explanation: The paper claims a specific group, L_{F2}(1,2)^×, is nonsofic. Lean asserts only existence of some finitely presented nonsofic group, which is a weaker existential conclusion with no link to the Leavitt unit group. That this group is finitely presented is not in the excerpt.
flags.probe_idea: State nonsoficity (with corrected Sofic) of the unit group of an explicit FreeAlgebra quotient over ZMod 2 by the Leavitt relations.

flags.explanation: The paper defines soficity for countable groups; Lean imposes no countability. This is harmless here because finitely presented groups are countable.
